Key points: Sunlight contains all visible wavelengths. As it enters the atmosphere, molecules (N₂, O₂) scatter shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) much more than longer wavelengths (red/orange) — scattering intensity goes as 1/λ⁴. So the scattered light reaching our eyes from all directions is predominantly blue. (Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so we perceive blue.)
